item.title: Kuwait Set to Issue Dollar Bonds as Iran Strikes Batter Country
item.description: Kuwait, under daily missile and drone attacks from Iran over the past two weeks, is aiming to sell dollar bonds on Wednesday.

item.title: Indian Drugmakers Rattled by Trump’s 100% Levy on Generic Drugs
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s plan to impose steep tariffs on generic medicines has unsettled Indian drugmakers and put the spotlight on their strategy in their biggest export market.

item.title: UK Stocks an Underappreciated AI Play, Brooks Macdonald CIO Says
item.description: The UK is an underappreciated knowledge-sector superpower and remains a “happy zone” for active stock-picking, according to William Hobbs, chief investment officer at Brooks Macdonald Asset Management.

item.title: France’s Deficit to Widen as Economic Growth Slows, IMF Says
item.description: The International Monetary Fund said France’s budget deficit will widen this year as the economy is hobbled by rising costs from the Iran war.

item.title: Alphabet Earnings Need to Show Cloud Growth as AI Spending Soars
item.description: With AI spending skyrocketing, investors are looking for Alphabet Inc.’s earnings to show strong growth in its cloud-computing business, which would demonstrate a clear return on the company’s investments.

item.title: Funds’ Bullish Wagers on European Gas Jump the Most Since War
item.description: Investment funds and other speculators boosted their net-long positions in European gas by the most since the first week of the Iran war, signaling a strong conviction that prices still have room to rise as the conflict darkens the supply outlook ahead of winter.

item.title: South African Inflation Overshoots, Cementing Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Traders hardened bets that the South African Reserve Bank will raise interest rates after annual inflation quickened more than expected in June.

item.title: MSEDCL Said to Pick Banks for India IPO Worth Up to $1 Billion
item.description: Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co., the power distribution company in India’s richest state, has shortlisted six investment banks for a planned initial public offering that could raise between $500 million and $1 billion, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: China Clings to Austerity Despite Intensifying Economic Slowdown
item.description: China’s public spending plunged last month by the most since October, suggesting the government tightened fiscal policy further despite increasing calls for more support as economic growth slips.

item.title: Indonesia Opts for Investor Perks Over Rate Hike to Boost Rupiah
item.description: Indonesia’s central bank left its benchmark interest rate unchanged, shifting its strategy from an aggressive monetary tightening campaign to offering a raft of new incentives to support the rupiah.

item.title: TPG Eyes Sale to Japan Hotel REIT for $860 Million
item.description: Investment fund TPG Asia Real Estate plans to sell a Tokyo hotel property to Japan Hotel REIT Investment Co. as a tourism boom unfolds and boosts valuations, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: BOJ Is Said Open to Faster Rate Hike Pace as Yen Adds Risks
item.description: Bank of Japan officials are open to raising interest rates at a faster pace than the consensus among economists, as the yen’s continued weakness adds to upside inflation risks, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Chicken Back on Menu as Cyber-Hit Nichirei Restores Operations
item.description: Tokyo-based food producer and distributor Nichirei Corp. says it will fully resume operations this week after a cyber attack disrupted its food delivery services, affecting clients nationwide including Kentucky Fried Chicken Japan.

item.title: Tencent Slides Most in Over a Year, Leading China Gaming Selloff
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd. fell the most in over a year, dragging Chinese gaming stocks lower as investors grew concerned about its mobile gaming business and some funds rotated back into AI-related names.

item.title: JPY/USD: Why Is Japan Yen So Weak? Can Government Intervention Help Currency?
item.description: The yen’s weakness has become a growing issue for Japan’s policymakers, given its role in driving up import prices and household living costs.

item.title: Middle East Shipping Threats Rise as Owners Plot Best Course
item.description: Challenges to shipping in the Middle East escalated, as a call from Iran-backed Houthi rebels against servicing Saudi ports spurred unusual maneuvers in the Red Sea, while a European Union naval group raised its threat level for the waterway.

item.title: Rubio, Jaishankar Urge Trade Deal Despite Pharma Tariff Threat
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar reinforced the importance of concluding an interim trade agreement between their two countries during a meeting in Manila on Wednesday.

item.title: UK Inflation Fell More Than Forecast in June on Cheaper Petrol
item.description: Cheaper motor fuel helped bring down UK inflation to the lowest in over a year, delivering some relief for households as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham promises to tackle the cost of living.

item.title: Rare Earths Giant Lynas Shares Fall to Five-Month Low After Revenue Miss
item.description: Lynas Rare Earths Ltd. shares dropped to a five-month low after Australia’s largest rare-earths producer reported quarterly sales that missed analysts’ expectations.

item.title: South Africa Finance Chief Set to Remove PIC Chairman, N24 Says
item.description: South Africa’s finance chief is preparing to oust his deputy from the position of chairman of the board of the Public Investment Corp., the state pension fund manager that’s been wracked by corruption and instability, News24 reported.

item.title: Copper Wavers Near $14,000 as Traders Watch for Trump’s Tariff
item.description: Copper pulled back from its highest level since early June as traders watched for any announcement from the White House on its plans for import tariffs on the metal.

item.title: Finland Seeks to Revive Economy, Handle Public Debt Under EU Pressure
item.description: Four years ago, Venla Malinen’s professors assured her that she had made the right decision to study construction architecture in the Finnish city of Kuopio. When she entered the workforce, they told her, there would be more opportunities than she and her classmates could handle.

item.title: Gas-Rich Australian Region Backs $28 Billion Data Center Project
item.description: Australia’s Northern Territory has granted land to a major data center project that claims it could attract A$40 billion ($28 billion) in private investment.

item.title: Japan 40-Year Bond Sale Sees Strongest Demand Since March 2025
item.description: Japan’s 40-year government bond auction drew its strongest demand since March 2025 as investors were attracted to higher yields.

item.title: Wheat Gains On Black Sea Risks and Corn Hits Two-Month High
item.description: Wheat rose for a second session on escalating Black Sea tensions and worsening crop prospects.

item.title: Sony and Mitsubishi Set Up AI Vision Joint Venture for Factories
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric Corp. and Sony Group Corp. said they will set up a joint venture to provide factory automation services by combining their expertise in artificial intelligence and image sensors.

item.title: China’s ‘AI for All’ Offensive Defies US Containment Playbook
item.description: The rapidly increasing global competitiveness of China’s artificial intelligence models is ringing alarm bells in Washington, posing a new test for the standard protectionist playbook.

item.title: Rising Crude, US Rate-Hike Bets Counter Dollar Inflow Support for Rupee
item.description: The Indian currency has fallen about 2% from its June high.

item.title: Sri Lanka Holds Rates as US-Iran War Clouds Economic Outlook
item.description: Sri Lanka’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, balancing the need to bring inflation back to target while supporting economic growth as renewed conflict between the US and Iran clouds the global outlook.
